reports.title: J & J Snack Foods Reports Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter Results

desk.headline: Sales down 1% to $406.0m, above estimates; adjusted EPS down 12% on freight costs; growth expected in fiscal 2027
results: Sales slipped 1% to $406.0m: Food Service fell 7.4% as planned bakery cuts outweighed churro and pretzel growth, while Retail rose 17.1% and Frozen Beverages 6.1%.
Gross margin widened to 33.7% from 31.7% on Project Apollo plant savings, mix and cheaper raw materials.
Freight and fuel pushed distribution costs up 21.6%, so adjusted EPS fell to $1.39 from $1.58; GAAP EPS of $1.80 was lifted by a $16m insurance gain from the Holly Ridge fire.
For the full year, sales fell 4% to $1.52bn and adjusted EPS to $4.04 from $4.27.
Year-end cash was $90.3m with no long-term debt; the company bought back $74.7m of shares in fiscal 2026.

guidance.summary: No numeric forecast in the release; the company expects sales to grow again in fiscal 2027 and a new phase of Project Apollo to add about $5m of yearly savings. On the call, management pointed to low-to-mid single-digit sales growth.

points: Price increases averaging about 2.5% take effect in January, about 3% for ICEE and Dippin' Dots.
Freight costs are expected to stay high, with pressure in the first half before easing once the increase is lapped around mid-2027.
The bakery exits cost about 3 points of full-year sales growth; management said further product cuts are not planned for 2027.
Management hopes to hold gross margin around 32% or higher in fiscal 2027, with ingredient inflation building in Q2 and Q3.
Retail Dippin' Dots sales were up more than 90% in tracked channels, and frozen beverage sales rose about 19% on cinema demand.
call.source: Q4 2026 call transcript — The Motley Fool, 18 Nov 2026

watch: Whether sales return to growth as the January price increases take hold.
Freight and fuel costs, and whether distribution expenses ease in the second half.
Gross margin holding near 32% as ingredient costs rise.
